plants.name: Cherry Tomato
plants.description: Prolific and forgiving, cherry tomatoes produce heavily even in containers on a sunny patio.

plants.name: Zucchini
plants.description: One or two plants can produce more squash than a household can eat, making it a huge cost-saver.

plants.name: Bush Beans
plants.description: Fast-growing and low-maintenance, bush beans don't need staking like pole varieties.

plants.name: Leaf Lettuce
plants.description: Ready in under a month and can be harvested a few leaves at a time for continuous salads.

plants.name: Bell Pepper
plants.description: Slower to establish but rewards patience with peppers that are expensive to buy fresh.

plants.name: Carrots
plants.description: Needs loose, rock-free soil, but home-grown carrots taste noticeably sweeter than store-bought.

plants.name: Cucumber
plants.description: Grows quickly on a trellis, saving ground space while producing a steady summer harvest.

plants.name: Basil
plants.description: A few plants replace expensive grocery-store herb packets all summer long.

plants.name: Mint
plants.description: Grows so aggressively it's best kept in its own container, but virtually never fails.

plants.name: Rosemary
plants.description: Drought-tolerant and perennial in mild climates, giving you fresh rosemary year after year.

plants.name: Spinach
plants.description: Thrives in cooler weather and is one of the fastest greens to reach harvest size.

plants.name: Radish
plants.description: One of the fastest vegetables you can grow, making it great for beginners and impatient gardeners.

plants.name: Strawberry
plants.description: A perennial patch pays off in year two and beyond, replacing pricey grocery-store berries.

plants.name: Kale
plants.description: Cold-hardy and productive well into fall, often outlasting other greens in the garden.

plants.name: Sweet Potato
plants.description: Needs a long warm season, but a single bed can yield pounds of storable, budget-friendly potatoes.

plants.name: Thyme
plants.description: A hardy, low-water perennial herb that keeps producing with almost no attention.
